newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kun Young creditors to extend aid.
newsitem.headline: Kun Young creditors to extend aid.

text.p: Creditors of South Korea's Kun Young Construction have agreed to extend emergency funds to help finance the debt-ridden company escape bankruptcy, a spokesman for the major creditor SEOULBANK said on Tuesday.
Creditors, comprising 14 banks and 21 other financial institutions, will grant soft loans to Kun Young when the company is due to redeem its debts.
But the terms and conditions of the emergency loans have not yet been decided. "It will be decided after we consult with the court," the spokesman added.
The decision followed a South Korean court's decision on Monday approving Kun Young's application for protection from its creditors.
SEOULBANK earlier said the bank would not extend any further credit to the company.
"As the company went into court protection, we have to consider the difficulties that Kun Young's subcontractors might face," the spokesman said.
"We decided to do our best to support Kun Young until the company can find a buyer," the spokesman said.
The construction company was rescued from debt default in early August by SEOULBANK, which extended emergency loans.
Since then, the home builder has been in takeover talks with a number of interested parties. Kun Young's current liabilities amounted to 550 billion won with assets of 800 billion won.
Kun Young is the second major construction group to collapse this year. Woosung Construction was taken over by the Hanil Group this January.
The home building industry is in a prolonged slump caused by falling real estate prices and excessive business expansion.
